claims.text: AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles can be investigated at the atomic scale using exsolution of CoFe alloy nanoparticles.
CoFe alloy nanoparticles are exsolved from La0.4Sr0.6Co0.2Fe0.7Mo0.1O3−δ.
The CoFe/La0.4Sr0.6Co0.2Fe0.7Mo0.1O3−δ system exhibits efficient CO2 electrolysis.
The material being investigated is AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Exsolution of CoFe alloy nanoparticles is the intervention applied to the AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticle system.
The proposed investigation is relevant under high-temperature application conditions.
An ABO3 structure is the structural mediator of the proposed behavior.
Exsolution contributes to a reintegration process during catalysis in the La0.4Sr0.6Co0.2Fe0.7Mo0.1O3−δ ABO3 system.
A reintegration process during catalysis explains the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The proposed intervention will produce efficient CO2 electrolysis.
The proposed method is applicable within high-entropy alloy design.
The thermal behavior obtained using exsolution should be compared with results from current methods.

contradictions.description: The initial material is free-standing AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, whereas the intervention and ABO3 mediator describe exsolution of CoFe nanoparticles from a compositionally distinct La-Sr-Co-Fe-Mo oxide; no relation between these systems is specified.
The stated objective concerns high-temperature thermal behavior, but the predicted outcome is CO2 electrolysis efficiency rather than a thermal-stability or structural-evolution measurement.
